significance: An old Vaishnava shrine at Diggi in Tonk district, rebuilt in 1527, and one of Rajasthan's larger pilgrimage centres. Devotees hold the water offered here to cure skin disease.
story: King Digva, struck with leprosy, is said to have recovered his health after recovering an image of Vishnu from the sea and installing it at Diggi, and the god was thereafter called Kalyanji, the benevolent one.
